parole.testo: From Aramaic ארדיכלא, from Akkadian 𒀵𒂍𒃲 (arad ēkalli, “slave of the palace”). Cognate with Classical Syriac ܐܪܕܝܟܠܐ (ʾardēḵlāʾ).
Borrowed from Aramaic אוּמָּנָא (ʾūmmānā, “artist, artisan, craftsman”) (Classical Syriac ܐܽܘܡܳܢܳܐ), from Akkadian 𒌝𒈪𒀀 (UM.MI.A /⁠ʾummānu⁠/, “expert, artisan, artist, craftsman, foreman”).

Borrowed from Aramaic אַסְפַּסְתָּא (ʾaspastā) / ܐܰܣܦܷܣܬܳܐ (ʾaspestā, “lucerne”), from Akkadian 𒊍𒉺𒊍𒋾 (aspastu, “presumably lucerne”), from Old Median *aspāstiš (“lucerne”), from Proto-Iranian *HacwaHastiš (“lucerne”, literally “horse-food”) from Proto-Iranian *Hácwah (“horse”) + Proto-Indo-European

Borrowed from Aramaic חָבִיתָא (ḥāḇīṯā, “jug, amphora”), as are also Arabic خَابِيَة (ḵābiya) and Ge'ez ኅበይ, ሕበይ (ḫəbäy, ḥəbäy), ultimately from Akkadian 𒂁𒉺𒅁𒌉 (ḫābû, ḫāpû, “jug, amphora”) of obscure origin.

parole.significato: wall: a structure serving as the exterior or a divider of a larger structure
parole.testo: Uncertain, theories include: * Borrowed from Aramaic כּוּתְלָא/ܟܘܬܠܐ, itself borrowed from Akkadian 𒄘𒋻 (/⁠kutallu⁠/, “behind, back of the head, backside, rear part of a structure”). * From Hittite [Term?] (/⁠kutt-⁠/, “wall”) + אֵל (el, “God, El, deity”).
From Aramaic כַּמֹּונָֹא / ܩܰܡܽܘܢܳܐ (kammōnā, “cumin”), from Akkadian 𒂵𒈬𒉡 (Ú.GAMUN /⁠kamūnu⁠/, “cumin”). Compare Ge'ez ከሚን (kämin), ካሚን (kamin), Arabic كَمُّون (kammūn).

Borrowed from Aramaic מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא (mashkantá, “mortgaging”), a cognate of Classical Syriac ܡܫܟܢܐ (meškānā, “pledge”). Both of them are in turn borrowed from Akkadian maškānum (“dwelling place, deposit”).

parole.significato: fish, found mostly in compounds to form names of sea creatures.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Aramaic נוּנָא (nūnā, “fish”), ultimately possibly from Akkadian 𒄩 (nūnum), possibly from Sumerian.

Ultimately from Old Aramaic שושמא (šūššmā), shortening of שומשומא (šumššemā), from Akkadian 𒃻𒈦𒌑𒈬 (/⁠šamaššammū⁠/), 𒊭𒈦𒌑𒈨 (/⁠šamaššammi⁠/, literally “oil plant”), compound of 𒉌 (/⁠šaman⁠/, “oil”) and 𒌑 (/⁠šammu⁠/, “plant”).
